question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` allow scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and what exact wildcard grammar is acceptable for Gateway browser-origin authorization?
rationale: The request broadens which browser origins may reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket handling, and current code/docs intentionally expose only exact full-origin matches plus the global allow-all `*`.

options.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
options.body: Define a small approved grammar such as Chrome-extension-only hosted opaque origins, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allow/reject cases before merge.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Leave scheme wildcards unsupported and focus related PRs on exact non-standard-origin matching, accepting that extension ID churn remains an operator burden.

options.title: Defer to broader origin-pattern design
options.body: Wait for the loopback pattern work to settle and decide whether extension scheme wildcards belong in the same contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
recommendation.body: Define a small approved grammar such as Chrome-extension-only hosted opaque origins, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allow/reject cases before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current Gateway origin-check boundary and is the strongest history-backed routing candidate for this security/product choice.
